headline.title: Margaret Atwood says the problem with AI is ‘garbage in, garbage out’
headline.summary: Margaret Atwood expressed concerns about artificial intelligence during an interview at the Babell Literary and Cultural Festival in Porto, Portugal, emphasizing the principle of "garbage in, garbage out." She highlighted the importance of quality input data in AI systems and shared her own experiences with AI technology.

articles.title: Why is Apple asking me to pay more for Big Tech’s AI obsession?
articles.summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook attributed recent price increases across several products, including the 16-inch MacBook Pro and the 11-inch iPad Air, to the rising costs associated with the company's investments in artificial intelligence. He described the current pricing model as "unsustainable," leading to price hikes of up to $300 for some devices.

articles.title: The fittest founder in the room got cancer. Here’s how he used AI to fight back.
articles.summary: Connor Christou, a fitness-focused entrepreneur diagnosed with cancer, utilized AI by inputting his health data, including blood results and wearable outputs, into the AI model Claude to aid in his treatment. This approach allowed him to analyze and optimize his health regimen during his battle with the disease.

articles.title: Asian AI startups launch Mythos-like models as Anthropic’s export ban drags on
articles.summary: Asian AI startups are introducing models with capabilities similar to Mythos, circumventing the impact of ongoing export bans from U.S. companies like Anthropic. This development may significantly affect the market position of U.S. AI labs in the region.

articles.title: Apple Vision Pro exec is reportedly leaving for OpenAI
articles.summary: Paul Meade, the Apple vice president overseeing the Vision Pro headset, is reportedly departing the company to join OpenAI's hardware team. His move marks a significant shift in leadership within Apple's augmented reality division.

articles.title: Trump Admin releases Anthropic Mythos to be used by more than 100 US companies, agencies
articles.summary: The Trump administration has authorized over 100 U.S. companies and government agencies to utilize Anthropic's Mythos 5, allowing access for their non-American employees as well. This move aims to enhance AI capabilities across various sectors.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Mythos 5 is back
articles.summary: Anthropic's Mythos 5 has resumed operations for a select group of organizations following a two-week negotiation process with the Trump administration. The public-facing version, Fable 5, remains unavailable at this time.

articles.title: Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol: a next-generation model
articles.summary: OpenAI has previewed GPT-5.6 Sol, a next-generation AI model designed to enhance performance in coding, science, and cybersecurity. The model features an advanced safety stack to ensure improved safety and reliability in its applications.

articles.title: OpenAI limits GPT-5.6 rollout after government request, says restrictions shouldn’t be the norm
articles.summary: OpenAI has limited the rollout of GPT-5.6 following a government request, emphasizing that such restrictions should not become standard practice. The company argues that these measures hinder access to advanced tools for users, developers, and other stakeholders.

articles.title: OpenAI unveils GPT-5.6 amid US AI regulatory drama
articles.summary: OpenAI has released a limited preview of its new GPT-5.6 model suite, which includes three variants: Sol, Terra, and Luna. This announcement comes shortly after the Trump administration requested a staggered release of the model amid ongoing discussions about AI regulation in the US.

articles.title: Why everyone from OpenAI to SpaceX is building their own chips (and turning up the heat on Nvidia)
articles.summary: OpenAI has announced its development of a custom inference chip, Jalapeño, in collaboration with Broadcom, as part of a broader trend among companies like Google, Apple, and SpaceX to reduce reliance on Nvidia for AI chips. This shift indicates a growing movement towards diversifying chip suppliers in the AI industry.

articles.title: Trump Administration Allows Anthropic to Release Mythos to Select US Organizations
articles.summary: The Trump administration has authorized Anthropic to release its advanced AI model, Mythos, to a limited number of U.S. organizations, including companies and government agencies. This decision follows several weeks of negotiations between Anthropic and the White House.
